_meta.indication: OXLUMO is indicated for the treatment of primary hyperoxaluria type 1 (PH1) to lower urinary oxalate levels in pediatric and adult patients.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial; patients randomized 2:1 to lumasiran or placebo for 6 months (placebo-controlled period) followed by an extension.
pivotal_trials.population: Children ≥6 years of age and adults with primary hyperoxaluria type 1 (PH1) with relatively preserved kidney function.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Percent change in 24-hour urinary oxalate excretion from baseline to Month 6 (LS means averaged from Months 3 to 6).
pivotal_trials.result: LS mean percent change in 24-hour urinary oxalate at Month 6 of -65 (lumasiran) vs -12 (placebo); between-group difference -54 (95% CI -62, -45); p < 0.0001.

pivotal_trials.population: Infants and children <6 years of age with PH1.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Percent change in spot urinary oxalate-to-creatinine ratio from baseline to Month 6 (LS means averaged from Months 3 to 6).
pivotal_trials.n: 16 patients in the efficacy population (18 in the safety population).
pivotal_trials.result: LS mean percent change in spot urinary oxalate-to-creatinine ratio at Month 6 of -71 (SEM 3; 95% CI -77, -65), consistent with ILLUMINATE-A.

key_safety: The most common adverse reaction (≥20%) was injection site reaction (38% vs 0% placebo); abdominal pain occurred more often with lumasiran (15%) than placebo (8%). Injection site reactions were generally mild and did not lead to discontinuation.
target_moa: Lumasiran is a double-stranded siRNA (conjugated to GalNAc) that, via RNA interference in hepatocytes, inhibits the mRNA of the hydroxyacid oxidase 1 (HAO1) gene, reducing glycolate oxidase (GO), thereby decreasing glyoxylate and downstream oxalate production.

advisory_committee.vote: No Advisory Committee meeting was held; the application did not raise significant issues regarding safety or effectiveness.

description.text: Changed indication to include lowering of plasma oxalate levels in adult and pediatric patients with primary hyperoxaluria type 1 (PH1)

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for a change to the currently approved indication to include lowering of plasma oxalate levels in adult and pediatric patients with primary hyperoxaluria type 1 (PH1).

basis.text: Breakthrough Therapy designation granted February 23, 2018 for PH1 based on marked and sustained reductions in urinary oxalate levels in a phase 2 study.

orphan_indication.text: Orphan drug designation granted February 8, 2016 for lumasiran for the treatment of PH1 (ODD 15-5053).
